papers.title: SPUX: Scalable Particle Markov Chain Monte Carlo for uncertainty quantification in stochastic ecological models
papers.abstract: Calibration of individual based models (IBMs), successful in modeling complex ecological dynamical systems, is often performed only ad-hoc. Bayesian inference can be used for both parameter estimation and uncertainty quantification, but its successful application to realistic scenarios has been hindered by the complex stochastic nature of IBMs. Computationally expensive techniques such as Particle Filter (PF) provide marginal likelihood estimates, where multiple model simulations (particles) are required to get a sample from the state distribution conditional on the observed data. Particle ensembles are re-sampled at each data observation time, requiring particle destruction and replication, which lead to an increase in algorithmic complexity. We present SPUX, a Python implementation of parallel Particle Markov Chain Monte Carlo (PMCMC) algorithm, which mitigates high computational costs by distributing particles over multiple computational units. Adaptive load re-balancing techniques are used to mitigate computational work imbalances introduced by re-sampling. Framework performance is investigated and significant speed-ups are observed for a simple predator-prey IBM model.

summary_zh.motivation: 实现复杂随机生态模型的贝叶斯推断与不确定性量化。
summary_zh.method: 采用并行粒子马尔可夫链蒙特卡洛算法，通过自适应负载均衡加速计算。
summary_zh.result: 在捕食-猎物模型中取得了显著的加速效果。
summary_zh.validation: 在简单生态模型上进行了数值验证。

summary_en.motivation: To enable Bayesian inference and uncertainty quantification for complex stochastic ecological models.
summary_en.method: A parallel implementation of Particle Markov Chain Monte Carlo with adaptive load balancing is proposed.
summary_en.result: Significant speed-ups are observed for a simple predator-prey individual-based model.
summary_en.validation: The method is validated on a numerical benchmark of a predator-prey IBM.
